title: MEN'S BASKETBALL | Chris Jans Postgame Radio Interview vs. Tulsa - 11/20/26
text: And let's start in the second half. I mean, it it was a tough offensive night for both of these teams. But Tulsa comes back from down 10. They tie it at 53. And then RJ Johnson gets six out of seven points on a 70 run for you. What did R.J. do for you down the stretch? >> Yeah, he used his frame, his body, his athleticism. Um, got downhill, got to the rim. We ran a little out of bounds play for him that we haven't run all year long, and he converted on that. And we needed that spurt. you know, Josh was trying to carry us there for a while in the second half and he needed a a robin, so to speak, and this particular night, it was R.J. who showed up and and was the robin uh in the second half. And you mentioned, you know, the offensive struggles on both teams. We actually played pretty well offensively in the second half. We had two turnovers. Uh we had what 10 or 11 for the game and two of them only in the second half. Our points per possession was 1.3. uh which you're going to win, you know, most games you play in if you can do that for 40 minutes now. But first half it was putrid and we were 088 and really struggling, but our defense kind of held in there in in the first half. But um I just told the guys, listen, I told told them before the game like I know this coach. I know this program that they're a great program and he's a really good coach and there's a very smart coach and they would have a great plan and it was going to be difficult and when we got up 10 I thought maybe and and they just wouldn't go away and they kept clawing back at us. So, um, in the end, like like always, when you win these type of games, you're going to learn and grow. And we just did that on the road at Central Florida, and now we got a neutral sight game where it wasn't easy and, um, we were able to get the W. >> You mentioned your defense. What do you like about the way you defended tonight? >> You know, again, we had a really good plan. Um, but when when they start seeing our plan, they adjust. you know, they had they did a really nice job of adjusting and so we had to adjust back, which we did. I felt pretty good about how we defended for the most part in the first half. Always want more, but um from a defensive uh cap, it was pretty good. Other than we gave up too many, uh offensive rebounds, very disappointed in that. And that's been one of the things that we've been able to count on all year long is our rebounding efforts on both ends of the floor. And uh and I knew this would be our biggest challenge. You know, that's what they do, too. this particular group that coach Conle has, they're a very good rebounding team and I knew it would be a challenge for us and I thought we did just okay. Uh we had some big ones in the second half, but uh and then second half it became a different type game. You know, we were both playing small ball quite a bit. uh they decided to go small ball and then kind of threw away their main offense with this is a lot of zooms and uh you know like Princeton type uh offensive looks and they went to just spread it out ghost pass and follow play one-on-one um and so then you we obviously had to adjust to that there late too. There was a time where Indie Okafor when he was out there did some good things for you, but to your point, they adjust their lineup so you go smaller and you don't have a true five out there and Collingwood's out there. Kind of look like you were forced to play some different combos that you maybe wouldn't normally play at this time. Am I right there? >> Yeah, for sure. And but that's okay. We we've had to do that uh earlier. I don't even remember who it was, but we've done that already. Um so it wasn't foreign to us. And just got to kind of tweak some of the offensive sets. That's the biggest problem. It's not the defensive end, it's the offensive end when you're trying to run some plays where guys don't, you know, get reps at threes and fours when they're ones and twos. And so, you got to kind of do it on the white board and talk them through it on the dead ball. But, um, you know, our staff and, uh, Alex in particular offensively does a good job with that. >> We talked about RJ, we talked about RJ, we talked about Josh Kimmani had a double double for you tonight. How big were some of the rebounds he got for you in the second half? >> I love coaching that kid, man. I do. I I so enjoy coaching Kamani Hamilton. It's been a joy to have him back and knock on wood, he'll be here all year long for us. And um [clears throat] he's just grimy. You know, we talked before the game, we want to be a a grimy, nastier team. And you know, we're not there yet. You know, that's the personality I want them to adopt. You know, um hopefully someday, you know, this year people will start looking at these guys as some junkyard dogs. We're not there. We're not close to there. But that's kind of what we're trying to do. And I think this team is built for it. I really do. I think we have what it takes to be that kind of team, but we're not there yet. But come on, he is. You know, I'd like them to uh play like him a little bit more and we use him as an example plenty of times and a lot of talk about Josh before this game and rightfully so and he had a nice moment with his family. It was really cool to be a small part in it. But uh extremely happy for Kamani to be home play in front of his family and friends and then obviously the way you played uh was kind of a you know carried on top. >> Well, you're getting ready to go to the Bahamas now for two more good tests. Wake Forest will be the first one in that opening game. With regard to your guys having their brains wired the way you wanted them to, did you see what you wanted there tonight? Can you build off that going forward? >> I think so. Um, they were positive uh probably more than I was. Uh, they were uh together. They had no issues uh with, you know, timeouts or how they communicated with one another. And you know the drill. Coaches always want more, you know. Um, and it's just what I really talked about in the locker room again is just how much everybody I I told him, think about what we do. Think about what we do from June until November. All the time, all the resources, all the pouring into each other and the and the time and the and the practices and the weights and the conditioning. And then you get to November and you only get 32 of these over what, a fourmon span and some change. And everybody's doing the same thing across the country. Everybody's pouring into it. And so these games are like Super Bowls. I've been talking about that for years in terms of how we prepare. But I need this team to understand it and adopt that mentality that we're playing the Super Bowl against Tulsa tonight in Jackson, Mississippi. Right. And then on Wednesday, we're going to play Wake Forest in the Super Bowl in the Bahamas. It doesn't matter where you play, you have to adopt that mentality and something we're going to continue to work on with this team. >> Congratulations. back-to-back wins away from home. Best of luck in the Bahamas next week.
